Read the tables of a group comparison

Source: R/compare_lsa.R
as.data.frame.lsa_comparison.Rd

as.data.frame() returns the tables of a group comparison from compare_lsa() or bayes_compare_lsa() as a plain data frame, and print() shows a short summary of the comparison. A comparison holds two tables, chosen with what: the comparison of every transition and the omnibus result for the structure as a whole. The per-transition table is the one transitions() reads; use transitions() when you want to keep only the significant transitions or order them by the size of the difference.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  what = c("edges", "global"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison_pairwise'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  what = c("edges", "global"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison_pairwise'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A comparison from compare_lsa() or bayes_compare_lsa() (class lsa_comparison or lsa_comparison_pairwise).

row.names, optional

Not used; present for consistency with the generic.

what

"edges" (default): one row per transition. "global": the omnibus result, one row per pair of groups.

...

Not used.

Value

as.data.frame() returns a data frame.

  • what = "edges": one row per transition (and per pair of groups when more than two groups were compared, with leading group_a, group_b columns); the columns are listed under Value in compare_lsa() and bayes_compare_lsa().

  • what = "global": one row per pair of groups with group_a, group_b and, for compare_lsa(), the omnibus statistic (sum of squared differences), its permutation p_value and either the number of permutations R (two groups) or the across-pairs adjusted p_adj (more than two groups); for bayes_compare_lsa(), n_credible, the number of credibly different transitions.

print() returns x invisibly.

See also

compare_lsa(), bayes_compare_lsa(), transitions().

Examples

g <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
         time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
cmp <- compare_lsa(g, R = 50, adjust = "BH")
cmp
#> <lsa_comparison>
#>   groups:   High vs Low
#>   measure:  log_or difference (High - Low)
#>   R:        50 label permutations
#>   edges:    37 significant of 78 tested (adjust = BH)
#>   omnibus:  statistic = 79.48, p = 0.01961
as.data.frame(cmp, what = "global")
#>   group_a group_b statistic    p_value  R
#> 1    High     Low  79.47723 0.01960784 50
head(as.data.frame(cmp))
#>         from    to   log_or_a  log_or_b       diff     p_perm      p_adj
#> 1      adapt adapt -1.1833106 -3.167522  1.9842113         NA         NA
#> 2   cohesion adapt -0.7935888 -3.920901  3.1273126 0.01960784 0.04133545
#> 3  consensus adapt -1.2188354 -1.966624  0.7477882 0.09803922 0.15294118
#> 4 coregulate adapt  0.7781535 -1.076619  1.8547730 0.01960784 0.04133545
#> 5    discuss adapt  1.0099554  2.250717 -1.2407612 0.01960784 0.04133545
#> 6    emotion adapt -1.3519489 -3.102996  1.7510475 0.23529412 0.32198142
#>   significant
#> 1       FALSE
#> 2        TRUE
#> 3       FALSE
#> 4        TRUE
#> 5        TRUE
#> 6       FALSE
